result: The study analyzed a discovery cohort of 124 individuals (93 PDAC, 12 chronic pancreatitis, 8 IPMN, 11 healthy controls) and validated findings in an independent cohort of 36 subjects (24 PDAC, 6 chronic pancreatitis, 6 IPMN). All subjects had biopsy-proven disease, with 30 early-stage and 63 advanced-stage PDAC patients in the discovery cohort.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly praised the cohort size, with one stating 'the strength of this study is in its numbers - the authors worked with a cohort of 124 cases, 93 of them which were PDAC samples, which considered large for an EV study.' Another reviewer noted the study 'presents a large cohort of plasma-derived extracellular vesicle samples from 124 individuals' and acknowledged validation 'in an external cohort.'

result: The EVtrap method was used for EV isolation, achieving >95% recovery yield with less contamination from soluble proteins. The method isolated particles with diameters between 100-200 nm (mean 152 nm), consistent with exosomes, as confirmed by TEM and nanoparticle tracking analysis. The study demonstrated feasibility of using EVtrap for discovery of hundreds of EV proteins from 100 µL plasma samples.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly endorsed the methodology, with one stating 'This study provides validation of assaying EVs using the novel EVtrap method (Extracellular Vesicles Total Recovery And Purification), which the authors show to be more efficient than current standard techniques and potentially more scalable for larger clinical studies.' The characterization data (TEM, NTA) was not questioned by any reviewer.

result: The proteomics workflow showed high technical reproducibility (r²>0.97 between replicates) and identified 1708 unique proteins in the discovery cohort, with an average of 912 EV proteins per 100 µL plasma sample. No differences were observed in the overall number of EV proteins between tumor and non-tumor samples or across different PDAC disease stages.
evaluation: Reviewers did not question the technical quality or reproducibility of the proteomics data. One reviewer noted 'the strength of evidence is solid,' implicitly accepting the technical aspects of the proteomics profiling. The high correlation between replicates and comprehensive protein identification were not challenged.

result: Differential expression analysis identified 207 proteins distinguishing pancreatic diseases from controls, with 182 proteins differentially expressed between PDAC and benign diseases. PDCD6IP, SERPINA12, and RUVBL2 showed remarkable overexpression (>10-fold) in PDAC. PCA and clustering analyses showed clear separation between PDAC and benign diseases, with PDAC patients segregating into early-stage and advanced-stage subgroups.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirmed these findings, stating 'Proteins they've identified as associated with pancreatic cancer over benign disease included PDCD6IP, SERPINA12 and RUVBL2.' The differential expression results and clustering patterns were accepted without critique, and reviewers noted the authors 'were not only able to identify candidate biomarkers for diagnosis that clearly stood out in the PDAC cohort.'

result: Analysis of metastatic versus non-metastatic PDAC identified 85 differentially expressed proteins. PSMB4, RUVBL2, and ANKAR were increased in metastatic disease, while RAP2B, SERPINA12, and IGLV4-69 were decreased. Supervised clustering showed clear separation between metastatic and non-metastatic cases.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly acknowledged these findings, stating 'They were even able to identify a set of EV proteins associated with metastasis and poorer prognosis, which include the proteins PSMB4, RUVBL2 and ANKAR.' The metastasis-associated protein signatures were accepted as valid discoveries without any expressed concerns.

result: Survival analysis identified that cEV expression of RALB, CRP, and CD55 significantly correlated with poor overall survival, while PDCD6IP expression was associated with improved outcomes.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirmed these prognostic findings, noting 'CRP, RALB and CD55' as proteins correlating with 'poorer prognosis.' The survival correlations were presented as accepted discoveries without any reviewer concerns about the analysis or interpretation.

result: A seven-protein EV signature (RUVBL2, PDCD6IP, ATP5F1, DLD, KRT20, CCT4, SERPINA12) was developed that achieved 100% accuracy in the discovery cohort and 89% prediction accuracy in the independent validation cohort for distinguishing PDAC from benign pancreatic diseases.
evaluation: Reviewers strongly endorsed this result, stating 'Their 7-EV protein signature yielded an 89% prediction accuracy for the diagnosis of PDAC against a background of benign pancreatic diseases that is compelling and comparable to other studies in the literature.' The validation in an independent cohort was specifically praised, with reviewers noting the authors 'validate it in an independent cohort of 36 new subjects.'

result: Individual markers did not achieve sufficiently high sensitivity and specificity compared to the combined seven-protein model for PDAC diagnosis.
evaluation: This finding was implicitly accepted by reviewers who praised the multi-marker approach and did not question the superiority of the combined model over individual markers. The reviewers' emphasis on the '7-EV protein signature' performance suggests acceptance of the need for a multi-marker panel.

result: KRT20 (keratin 20), a gastrointestinal epithelia-associated keratin, was increased in PDAC patient EVs, while basal cell-associated keratins (KRT4, KRT15, KRT3) were reduced. KRT20 overexpression is frequently found in pancreatic tumor tissues and correlates with poor prognosis.
evaluation: Reviewers did not question these specific keratin findings. The identification of KRT20 as part of the broader differential expression analysis was implicitly accepted through reviewers' general endorsement of the biomarker discoveries and their statement that the study identified 'both new and known proteins of interest.'

result: Pathway analysis revealed proteins involved in metabolism, immune regulation, protein binding, exocytosis, endocytosis, and cellular protein localization in circulating EVs. Immunological functions showed complex regulation with increased leukocyte-mediated immunity and degranulation but decreased Fc receptor signaling and complement activation. Direct profiling of cEVs provided unique insights into systemic changes in immune biology during pancreatic cancer development.
evaluation: Reviewers did not challenge the pathway analysis findings or the interpretation about systemic immune changes. The general statement that 'the strength of evidence is solid' and acceptance of the comprehensive proteomics profiling implicitly supports these pathway-level observations, though reviewers did not specifically discuss them.

result: The EV proteomic profiles of PDAC patients exhibited significant heterogeneity, with marker abundances varying significantly between individual patients, highlighting the need to develop multi-protein panels for pancreatic cancer diagnosis and prognosis.
evaluation: Reviewers implicitly accepted this observation through their endorsement of the multi-marker approach. The statement that 'no single marker achieved sufficiently high sensitivity and specificity as the combined model' was not questioned, supporting the authors' interpretation about heterogeneity and the need for multi-protein panels.

result: The single-center nature of the study is an inherent limitation. Validation with a larger cohort of controls would be ideal for greater statistical power, and the seven EV protein PDAC panel should be cross-validated in larger and multicenter populations.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly identified this limitation, stating 'The limitations of this study are its containment within a single institution - further studies are warranted to apply the authors' 7-EV protein PRAC panel to multiple other cases at other institutions in a larger cohort.' Reviewers also noted 'The benign disease group (n=20) and healthy control groups (n=11) were relatively small.'

result: There may be some degree of heterogeneity in the extracellular vesicles analyzed using EVtrap and mass spectrometry, and the clinical impact of identified biomarkers will need cross-validation using other methods.
evaluation: Reviewers did not explicitly discuss EV heterogeneity concerns but implicitly accepted this limitation through their call for further validation. The general acknowledgment that 'further studies are warranted' aligns with the authors' recognition of methodological limitations requiring cross-validation.

result: This study represents the largest proteomics profiling dataset of circulating EVs in pancreatic cancer to date, providing a valuable resource with a comprehensive catalog of novel proteins. The study identified and validated new EV markers distinguishing PDAC from benign pancreatic diseases and discovered cEV proteins associated with metastatic disease and poor prognosis.
evaluation: Reviewers strongly endorsed the study's contribution, stating 'the authors worked with a cohort of 124 cases, 93 of them which were PDAC samples, which considered large for an EV study.' They affirmed the study 'adds to the growing body of evidence in using EVs for earlier detection of pancreatic cancer, identifying both new and known proteins of interest' and has 'promising value to scientists and clinicians.'

result: The seven EV protein signature with 89% prediction accuracy serves as proof-of-concept with potential to facilitate biomarker test development. Higher diagnostic performance is needed for clinical use, and future studies should investigate combining cEV proteins with other biomarkers (cell-free DNA, serum proteins, metabolites) as a multi-analyte assay. The methodological advance can be adopted for biomarker discovery in other cancer types.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledged the promising results but implicitly recognized limitations in clinical applicability. While praising the 89% accuracy as 'compelling and comparable to other studies,' reviewers emphasized the need for 'further studies' and validation in 'larger and multicenter populations,' suggesting the current performance may not yet meet clinical standards. The speculative nature of future applications was not directly evaluated.
